answer_raw:
Top cities vary depending on whether you prioritize economic power or purely livable environments, with **New York** taking the top spot for overall global influence while European cities like **Vienna** lead in specific quality of life metrics. 

The rankings depend entirely on the methodology used by the research firms:

**Oxford Economics (2026 Global Cities Index)** — This index ranks 1,000 cities across four categories: economics, human capital, environment, and quality of life [2][4]. In the overall ranking, **New York** is No. 1 as of October 2026 [2]. While the US has eight cities in the top 20, the quality of life category (which accounts for 25% of the score) is not a strength for the US, with only one US city making that specific cut [2]. **Canberra** also performs well in the quality of life category, though it ranks 45th overall [8].

**EIU (Global Liveability Index)** — This index assesses 173 cities across five categories: stability, healthcare, culture and environment, education, and infrastructure [1]. The average liveability score across all cities is **76.1 out of 100** as of July 2026 [1].

**Monocle (Quality of Life 2026)** — This survey uses correspondent judgment to assess safety, connectivity, governance, and green space [7]. As of July 2026, North American cities have struggled due to crime, inequality, and housing issues, making cities like **Perth** more attractive [7].

**Mercer (Quality of Living Survey)** — Historically, this survey has ranked **Vienna** as the best place to live, followed by **Zurich** and **Auckland** [3]. In 2020, **Prague** was ranked 69th globally and topped the rankings for Central and Eastern Europe [5].
